Subject: Thanks for the call — Pricing & latency follow-up

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Use case: customer support summarization + real-time chat assistance for power users (short responses ~40-120 tokens, occasional long summaries ~800-1,200 tokens).
- Current volume estimate: 25k active users, avg 2 requests/user/day => ~50k requests/day. Expected token mix: 85% short (avg 80 tokens), 15% long (avg 1,000 tokens).
- Ballpark monthly token estimate: ~2.5M short tokens/day * 30 ~75M + long tokens ~7.5M => ~82.5M tokens/month. (Open to refinement.)

Key asks from us:
1) Target unit economics: you mentioned target of ~$15-25 / 1M tokens — can you confirm a target $/1M tokens and if that needs to include streaming or just completed-response pricing?
2) Latency SLOs: what percentile + target matters (p50/p95/p99)? You called out needing <300ms p95 for the short responses in the widget.
3) Procurement timing and budget range for Q1 2027.

Attached: initial estimation workbook and a small latency vs cost cheat sheet. I'll loop in Dev for technical routing questions.

Next: I can send a dedicated proposal with 3 pricing/latency options (cost-optimized, balanced, SLO-focused) once you confirm the $/1M target and p95 SLA.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is great, very aligned. A few clarifications: 

- We were aiming for a target of $18 / 1M tokens as a starting negotiation point. That needs to cover request/response tokens; streaming can be priced the same unless you require separate metering.
- Latency: for the in-app short responses we need <= 300ms p95. For background jobs (batch summarization) latency isn't strict.
- Budget range for pilot (Q1): $30k-$50k committed spend for the first quarter, scaling to ~$150k/mo if pilot metrics look good.

Two asks:
1) Can you outline specifically which product tier / Dedicated sizing would meet the p95 requirement?
2) Any suggestions on batching/streaming configurations to hit that p95 while keeping unit cost near $18/1M?

I'll introduce our procurement lead separately for contracting.

—Sara

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — Pricing & latency follow-up

Perfect — thanks for confirming the $18/1M target and the pilot budget range. High-level proposal:

Option A — Cost-optimized:
- Hosted, standard tier with aggressive batching and prefix caching
- Expected unit rate achieved by avg batching; estimated $12-16 / 1M tokens
- p95 expected ~450-600ms for short responses — likely not meeting 300ms requirement

Option B — Balanced (recommended):
- Dedicated small pool (reserved) with burst capacity; quantized model variant + continuous KV caching
- Estimated $16-20 / 1M tokens (can get to $18 with a 3-month pilot commit)
- p95 expected ~220-320ms depending on region and request routing

Option C — SLO-focused:
- Dedicated larger pool, reserved threads, and streaming enabled for short responses (lower inference latency at higher cost)
- Estimated $24-30 / 1M tokens
- p95 <= 200ms consistently

I asked Dev to confirm technical knobs for Option B to try to hit $18 and p95 ~300ms. See Dev's note below.

Next steps:
- Dev to confirm batch/stream settings and a concrete sizing recommendation for the Dedicated pool.
- I'll draft a three-option term sheet and a pilot PO template for Procurement.

Thanks — will follow up with the doc and a short one-pager.

Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sara Lang <sara@fintechai.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — Pricing & latency follow-up

Hi Sara — quick technical write-up to align expectations for Option B (balanced):

- Model & variant: Use a quantized 8-bit variant of a curated LLM we verified for semantic accuracy on short responses. Quantization reduces GPU memory and cost but keeps quality high for short outputs.
- Serving tier: Dedicated small pool (2 x NVIDIA H100 equiv. capacity) with autoscale buffer to handle spikes. Pool sizing aimed at sustaining ~1,200 concurrent short requests with KV prefix caching.
- Batching settings: continuous batching with a max batch latency of 20ms and max batch size tuned to keep p95 <= 300ms. For this workload, target batch size 8-16 for short responses.
- Streaming: enable streaming for the widget responses to minimize perceived latency (first token delivered < 80ms). Note: streaming increases request overhead and can inflate token accounting slightly; we'll include that in the $/1M model.
- Routing: prefer regional routing to reduce network RTT; fall back to nearest compatible pool.

Estimated economics: with quantized variant + dedicated small pool + caching, we can approach $17.5 - $19 / 1M tokens at pilot volumes. Key levers to get to $18: tighten cache hit rates (client-side prefixing), accept small trade on model size, and commit to a 3-month reserved capacity.

I'll prepare a short sizing calc and an example throughput runbook and attach it to the proposal.

—Dev
